title: scan() and decode() diverge: consecutive terminator lines
description:
scan() and decode() return different is_truncated values for input with two consecutive terminator lines (backtick or space) before the end line.

Reproduction: Input b'begin 644 f\n#0V%T\n\x60\n\x60\nend\n'

decode(): first backtick triggers look-ahead over remaining lines. The second backtick is not b"end" and not empty (len=1), so the look-ahead loop breaks -> break outer -> is_truncated=true.

scan(): first backtick -> Ok(0) -> saw_terminator=true. Second backtick -> decode_line returns Ok(0) -> saw_terminator=true (already). "end" -> found_end=true -> is_truncated=false.

Confirmed by test: assertion 'decode.is_truncated == scan.is_truncated' fails with left=true, right=false.

Root cause: decode.rs look-ahead (lines 156-165) treats any non-empty non-"end" line after the terminator as malformed. scan.rs re-uses decode_line for post-terminator lines and only transitions to truncated on Ok(n>0) or Err, allowing multiple Ok(0) responses to chain indefinitely.

Impact: Callers using scan() then decode() on the same slice observe different is_truncated flags for the same block.

Fix: In scan.rs handle_block(), after the terminator is seen, accept only strictly-empty lines (b"") between terminator and end, matching decode.rs look-ahead semantics. Additional backtick/space lines should trigger truncation.
